components.note: 冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.

example.hanzi: 新学期从九月开始。
example.pinyin: Xīn xuéqī cóng jiǔyuè kāishǐ.
example.english: The new semester starts in September.
example.fact: The idea of a school calendar built around a long summer break traces back to 19th-century agrarian America, where children were needed to help harvest crops in the warm months. Many countries never adopted that pattern — Japan and South Korea, for instance, start their academic year in April, timed to the blooming of cherry blossoms rather than to any farm work.

components.note: 匸 (a box, a hiding place) — 匿 relates to concealment.
若 (ruò) gives a sound distantly related to 匿's reading nì, having drifted apart over time.
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 他匿名捐赠了一百万美元。
example.pinyin: Tā nìmíng juānzèng le yìbǎiwàn měiyuán.
example.english: He anonymously donated one million dollars.
example.fact: Since the 1930s, a group of mostly French mathematicians has published foundational textbooks on rigorous mathematics under a single invented name, Nicolas Bourbaki, so that no individual author's reputation would attach to the work. The group still exists today, and 'Bourbaki' has never corresponded to a real person.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — suggests a gesture, a beckoning motion.
召 depicts a call or summons — a hand gesture calling someone over gave 招 its meaning 'to beckon, to recruit.'
彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed

example.hanzi: 主人热情地招待了客人。
example.pinyin: Zhǔrén rèqíng de zhāodài le kèrén.
example.english: The host warmly entertained the guests.
example.fact: In traditional Bedouin culture of the Arabian Peninsula, hospitality carries the weight of law: a guest, even a stranger or former rival, must be sheltered and fed for three days without being asked their business. The custom, known as diyafa, is thought to have arisen from the harsh conditions of desert travel, where turning a traveler away could mean their death.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 评 relates to speaking judgments or opinions about something
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 评's reading píng
刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 裁判评判了这场比赛的结果。
example.pinyin: Cáipàn píngpàn le zhè chǎng bǐsài de jiéguǒ.
example.english: The referee judged the outcome of the match.
example.fact: After a vote-trading scandal at the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympics, the International Skating Union overhauled how figure skating is judged, replacing the old 6.0 scale with a detailed point system and, for a time, anonymous panels. The reform was meant to make scoring harder to manipulate, though critics still debate how much subjectivity it removed.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 我认得这条街,以前来过。
example.pinyin: Wǒ rènde zhè tiáo jiē, yǐqián láiguo.
example.english: I recognize this street — I've been here before.
example.fact: In 1971, neuroscientist John O'Keefe discovered 'place cells' in the rat hippocampus that fire only when the animal is in a specific location, effectively forming an internal map that lets it recognize where it has been. The discovery, later extended to a full model of spatial navigation, earned O'Keefe a share of the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — arrows were historically used as a measuring standard, tied to 短's meaning 'short.'
豆 (dòu) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading duǎn has diverged.
日 (sun, related to time) — 暂 describes a short span of time.
斩 (zhǎn) gives a sound close to zàn.

example.hanzi: 这次相遇十分短暂。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì xiāngyù shífēn duǎnzàn.
example.english: This encounter was very brief.
example.fact: Mayflies spend one to three years as aquatic nymphs but live as winged adults for only a few hours to a couple of days, just long enough to mate and lay eggs before dying. Their scientific order name, Ephemeroptera, literally reflects that fleeting adult stage.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'
寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'

example.hanzi: 导游引导我们参观了故宫。
example.pinyin: Dǎoyóu yǐndǎo wǒmen cānguān le Gùgōng.
example.english: The tour guide led us through the Forbidden City.
example.fact: The Eddystone Lighthouse off the English coast was destroyed by storms and fire three times before engineer John Smeaton rebuilt it in 1759 using interlocking granite blocks shaped like a tree trunk. That design became the standard for lighthouse construction worldwide for the next two centuries.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 工人正在安装新的空调。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài ānzhuāng xīn de kōngtiáo.
example.english: Workers are installing the new air conditioner.
example.fact: Willis Carrier built the first modern air conditioner in 1902, not for human comfort but to control humidity at a Brooklyn printing plant where damp air was blurring the ink. Home air conditioning didn't become common in the United States until the 1950s.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 荷 names the lotus plant.
何 (hé) gives the sound — an exact match with 荷.
A stylized drawing of orchid blossoms and leaves growing up from the ground.

example.hanzi: 荷兰以风车和郁金香闻名。
example.pinyin: Hélán yǐ fēngchē hé yùjīnxiāng wénmíng.
example.english: The Netherlands is famous for its windmills and tulips.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s, speculative prices for rare bulbs rose so high that by February 1637 a single bulb reportedly sold for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman. Economists still cite it as one of the earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逐 means to chase or pursue, involving movement.
豕 (shǐ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading zhú has diverged.
氵 (water) — 渐 relates to a gradual flow, like water advancing bit by bit.
斩 (zhǎn) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though it has diverged from the modern reading jiàn.

example.hanzi: 天色逐渐变暗了。
example.pinyin: Tiānsè zhújiàn biàn àn le.
example.english: The sky gradually grew dark.
example.fact: When Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, he suggested landmasses creep apart at roughly the rate fingernails grow, a few centimeters a year. Decades later, plate tectonics confirmed the mechanism and showed the drift is powered by convection currents deep in the Earth's mantle.

components.note: 彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
己 (a kneeling child) — the one being disciplined.
攵 (a hand with a stick) — correcting the child, giving 改 its meaning 'to change, correct, reform.'

example.hanzi: 他修改了论文的结论部分。
example.pinyin: Tā xiūgǎi le lùnwén de jiélùn bùfen.
example.english: He revised the conclusion section of his paper.
example.fact: Linus Torvalds wrote the Git version-control system in about two weeks in 2005, after a licensing dispute cut off the Linux kernel project's access to the commercial tool it had been using to track code revisions. Git went on to become the most widely used system for managing changes to software worldwide.

meanings: to withdraw the mandate of heaven
(separable verb sometimes used in the pattern 革noun的命)

components.note: 革 depicts an animal hide being stretched out and worked — the picture behind its meaning 'hide, leather, to reform.'
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.hanzi: 工业革命改变了整个世界。
example.pinyin: Gōngyè gémìng gǎibiàn le zhěnggè shìjiè.
example.english: The Industrial Revolution changed the entire world.
example.fact: The Industrial Revolution is usually dated from the 1760s, when James Watt's improvements made the steam engine efficient enough to power factories rather than just pump water out of mines. Within roughly a century, mechanized production had multiplied per-capita economic output in Britain far beyond anything seen in earlier human history.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn
覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'

example.hanzi: 每个人只能投一张选票。
example.pinyin: Měi gèrén zhǐ néng tóu yì zhāng xuǎnpiào.
example.english: Each person can only cast one ballot.
example.fact: The secret ballot is sometimes called the 'Australian ballot' because South Australia was among the first places to adopt it, in 1856, letting voters mark their choices in private rather than announce them aloud. The United States did not widely adopt the practice until the 1890s, largely to curb vote-buying and intimidation at the polls.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 岩 names the rock that makes up a mountain.
石 (rock/stone) — together with 山, the image of rock forming a mountain gave 岩 its meaning 'cliff, rock.'
口 (a rock) — the boulder itself.
厂 (a cliff) — the rock lying at the base of a cliff, the source of 石's meaning 'stone, rock.'

example.hanzi: 这块岩石有几百万年的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài yánshí yǒu jǐ bǎiwàn nián de lìshǐ.
example.english: This rock is millions of years old.
example.fact: The Acasta Gneiss, exposed along a riverbank in Canada's Northwest Territories, has been dated to about 4.02 billion years old, making it one of the oldest known intact rock formations on Earth's surface. It formed less than 600 million years after the planet itself.

components.note: Woman — an old semantic root sometimes linked to feelings.
Gives the sound jiān, related to xián but drifted apart over time.
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating

example.hanzi: 警方怀疑他有嫌疑。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng huáiyí tā yǒu xiányí.
example.english: Police suspect that he is a suspect.
example.fact: The modern polygraph, invented by police officer John Larson in 1921, measures changes in heart rate, breathing, and skin conductivity rather than lies directly. Its scientific validity remains disputed, and polygraph results are inadmissible as evidence in most courts in the United States today.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.
心 (heart) at the bottom shows this is about a state of mind.
或 (perhaps, maybe) above conveys uncertainty, giving 惑 its meaning 'to confuse, to be puzzled.'

example.hanzi: 这道题把我迷惑了。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí bǎ wǒ míhuo le.
example.english: This problem confused me.
example.fact: The Ames room, designed by ophthalmologist Adelbert Ames Jr. in 1946, uses a distorted, trapezoidal shape and forced perspective to trick viewers into seeing people appear to shrink or grow dramatically as they walk across it. The illusion works only when viewed through a single peephole that hides the room's true geometry.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 船 is a vessel that travels on water, directly tied to its meaning 'ship, boat'
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 船员们正在检查设备。
example.pinyin: Chuányuánmen zhèngzài jiǎnchá shèbèi.
example.english: The crew members are checking the equipment.
example.fact: The RMS Titanic carried roughly 885 crew members in 1912, more than half of whom died when the ship sank. The disaster directly led to the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) in 1914, which set standards, still in use today, for lifeboat capacity and onboard safety equipment.

components.note: 冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 她获得了博士学位。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdé le bóshì xuéwèi.
example.english: She earned a doctoral degree.
example.fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is generally regarded as the oldest continuously operating university in the world. Its early scholars helped establish the practice of formally examining students and granting degrees as recognized academic credentials.

components.note: A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'
氵 (water/stream) — the water being crossed.
步 (to step, walk) — feet moving through it, together giving 涉 its meaning 'to wade across' and, more broadly, 'to be involved in.'

example.hanzi: 请不要干涉我的私事。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bùyào gānshè wǒ de sīshì.
example.english: Please don't interfere with my private affairs.
example.fact: In 1801, Thomas Young shone light through two narrow slits and observed a striped pattern on a screen behind them, evidence that light waves were interfering with each other much like ripples on water. The double-slit experiment remains one of the clearest demonstrations that light behaves as a wave.

components.note: The oldest form of 前 showed a foot above a boat, the image of moving forward by sailing. Over centuries of stylization, that boat shape flattened into the strokes now read as 月/刀 at the bottom, no longer recognizable as a boat, leaving 前 as an essentially indivisible modern character standing for 'front, before.'
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 客人从前门进来了。
example.pinyin: Kèrén cóng qiánmén jìnlái le.
example.english: The guest came in through the front door.
example.fact: The oldest surviving wooden door in Europe, found at a Neolithic lake settlement near Zurich, Switzerland, has been dated to around 3063 BC and still has its original wooden pivot hinges intact. Archaeologists believe it once sealed the entrance to a stilt house built over the water.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
⺮ (bamboo) — early tallies and charms were carved on strips of bamboo.
付 (fù) gives a sound close to fú, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他的说法与证据相符。
example.pinyin: Tā de shuōfǎ yǔ zhèngjù xiāngfú.
example.english: His statement matches the evidence.
example.fact: In his 1892 book Finger Prints, Francis Galton showed that fingerprint patterns are distinctive enough that no two individuals, not even identical twins, had ever been found to share the same one. That work laid the statistical groundwork for using fingerprints to match suspects to crime scenes.

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of two originally distinct traditional characters, 發 (to issue, emit) and 髮 (hair). 發's older form combined a bow-and-arrow image with a stepping foot to suggest shooting something forth; simplification stripped those pictorial parts away, so the modern 发 no longer decomposes into meaningful pieces.
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.hanzi: 萤火虫在夜里发光。
example.pinyin: Yínghuǒchóng zài yèlǐ fāguāng.
example.english: Fireflies glow at night.
example.fact: Fireflies produce light through a chemical reaction between a molecule called luciferin and the enzyme luciferase inside specialized cells in their abdomens. The reaction converts chemical energy into light with almost none lost as heat, making it far more energy-efficient than an incandescent bulb.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
A stylized drawing of orchid blossoms and leaves growing up from the ground.

example.hanzi: 他从英格兰来到中国留学。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng Yīnggélán láidào Zhōngguó liúxué.
example.english: He came from England to study in China.
example.fact: Stonehenge, in southern England, was built in stages starting around 3000 BC, and some of its smaller bluestones were quarried in the Preseli Hills of Wales, more than 200 kilometers away. How Neolithic builders transported multi-ton stones that far, without wheels or draft animals, is still debated by archaeologists.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 泳 describes moving through water.
永 (yǒng) gives the sound — an exact match with 泳.
氵 (water) shows 池 relates to a body of water.
也 (yě) gives a sound distantly related to chí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在泳池里玩耍。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài yǒngchí lǐ wánshuǎ.
example.english: The children are playing in the swimming pool.
example.fact: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro, built around 2500 BC in the Indus Valley Civilization, is one of the earliest known public water tanks, with a brick-lined basin, waterproof mortar, and its own drainage system. Its exact purpose — ritual bathing, public use, or both — is still debated by archaeologists.

meanings: see 恆星系|恒星系[heng2 xing1 xi4]

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
糸 (thread/silk) — 系 relates to connecting or tying things together, like threads linking into a system.

example.hanzi: 银河系只是宇宙中众多星系之一。
example.pinyin: Yínhéxì zhǐshì yǔzhòu zhōng zhòngduō xīngxì zhī yī.
example.english: The Milky Way is just one of many galaxies in the universe.
example.fact: Estimates of how many galaxies exist have grown sharply as telescopes improved: analysis of deep Hubble Space Telescope images published in 2016 suggested the observable universe may contain roughly two trillion galaxies, about ten times higher than earlier estimates. Most of those galaxies are too faint or distant to be seen with current instruments.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 警方终于结案了。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhōngyú jié'àn le.
example.english: The police finally closed the case.
example.fact: The Golden State Killer case went unsolved for more than 40 years until 2018, when investigators uploaded DNA from an old crime scene sample to a public genealogy website and traced it through distant relatives to Joseph James DeAngelo. The technique, now called forensic genetic genealogy, has since helped close dozens of other cold cases.

components.note: Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'
又 (a hand) forms the frame of the character.
丶 (a small object) sits held within the hand — a hand grasping an object, giving 叉 its meaning 'fork, prong.'

example.hanzi: 两条路在这里交叉。
example.pinyin: Liǎng tiáo lù zài zhèlǐ jiāochā.
example.english: The two roads cross here.
example.fact: The first cloverleaf highway interchange in the United States was built in 1928 near Woodbridge, New Jersey, using looping ramps so that crossing roads could merge and diverge without a single traffic light. The design spread rapidly once the interstate highway system began construction in the 1950s.

components.note: 儿 (a standing person) — the figure being emphasized.
二 (an extra line at the top) — emphasizing the person's head, the 'first, foremost' part of them — the source of 元's meanings 'origin, first' and, by extension, the basic unit of Chinese currency.
自 here depicts a head (the character also independently means 'nose, self').
丷 depicts hair atop the head — 首 originally pictured a head with hair, giving its meaning 'head, chief, first.'

example.hanzi: 两国元首举行了会谈。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó yuánshǒu jǔxíng le huìtán.
example.english: The heads of the two states held talks.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II served as the United Kingdom's head of state for over 70 years, from 1952 to 2022, the longest verified reign of any female monarch in recorded history. Her reign spanned 15 British prime ministers, starting with Winston Churchill.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.
心 (heart) — 愿 relates to a heartfelt wish or desire
原 (yuán) gives a loose sound connection to 愿's reading yuàn

example.hanzi: 尊重每个人的意愿很重要。
example.pinyin: Zūnzhòng měi gèrén de yìyuàn hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: It's important to respect everyone's wishes.
example.fact: The 1947 Nuremberg Code, drafted after wartime medical atrocities were exposed at the Nuremberg trials, established that voluntary consent from research subjects is essential before any experiment can proceed. It became the founding document behind modern medical ethics rules on patient autonomy and informed consent.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.

example.hanzi: 电子邮件逐渐取代了传统信件。
example.pinyin: Diànzǐ yóujiàn zhújiàn qǔdài le chuántǒng xìnjiàn.
example.english: Email has gradually replaced traditional letters.
example.fact: Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built the first working digital camera prototype in 1975, but the company was slow to commercialize the technology it had invented, fearing it would undercut film sales. Digital cameras eventually replaced film almost entirely, and Kodak filed for bankruptcy protection in 2012.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — relates directly to 切's meaning 'to cut.'
七 (qī) gives a sound hint — 切 is pronounced qiè, sharing the same initial consonant.
阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'

example.hanzi: 医生切除了病人的肿瘤。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng qiēchú le bìngrén de zhǒngliú.
example.english: The doctor removed the patient's tumor.
example.fact: On October 16, 1846, surgeon John Collins Warren removed a tumor from a patient's neck at Massachusetts General Hospital while dentist William Morton administered ether gas, in what became known as the Ether Dome demonstration. It was one of the first public surgeries performed with general anesthesia, transforming surgery from an agonizing ordeal into a painless procedure.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 睡 relates to closing the eyes to sleep.
垂 (chuí) gives a sound partly close to shuì, sharing part of the rhyme.
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.

example.hanzi: 她穿着睡衣看电视。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe shuìyī kàn diànshì.
example.english: She is watching TV in her pajamas.
example.fact: Unlike most primates, which sleep in several short bouts scattered across the day and night, humans consolidate sleep into a single long block. Some researchers link this shift to our ancestors' controlled use of fire and shelter, which made it safer to sleep deeply through the night rather than stay half-alert against predators.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.
攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.

example.hanzi: 卫星接收到了地面信号。
example.pinyin: Wèixīng jiēshōu dào le dìmiàn xìnhào.
example.english: The satellite received the signal from the ground.
example.fact: When the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in October 1957, the satellite transmitted a simple radio beep that amateur radio operators around the world could pick up on ordinary shortwave receivers. That beep, audible to the public within hours of launch, is widely credited with kicking off the space age.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 警方保存了现场的证物。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng bǎocún le xiànchǎng de zhèngwù.
example.english: The police preserved the evidence from the scene.
example.fact: In 1988, Colin Pitchfork became the first person convicted of murder using DNA profiling, a technique developed a few years earlier by geneticist Alec Jeffreys at the University of Leicester. The same method also cleared an initial suspect who had falsely confessed to the crime, showing DNA evidence could exonerate as well as convict.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — suggests departing or leaving.
贵 (valuable, precious) — leaving something valuable behind gave 遗 its meaning 'to lose, to leave behind.'
心 (heart/mind) — 忘 relates to something slipping from the mind.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to wàng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 时间让人渐渐遗忘痛苦。
example.pinyin: Shíjiān ràng rén jiànjiàn yíwàng tòngkǔ.
example.english: Time gradually makes people forget pain.
example.fact: In the 1880s, psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus memorized lists of nonsense syllables and tested his own recall over time, finding that memory for new information drops sharply within the first hours after learning before leveling off. His results, later called the forgetting curve, remain a foundational finding in memory research.

components.note: 刀 is a pictograph of a single-edged blade, drawn as a curved line for the back of the blade with a small hook near the handle for the point — a shape close enough to a real knife's silhouette that the character has stayed largely unchanged for thousands of years.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他用刀子切水果。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng dāozi qiē shuǐguǒ.
example.english: He uses a knife to cut fruit.
example.fact: The Oldowan stone tools of East Africa, some dated to about 2.6 million years ago, are among the earliest known deliberately shaped cutting implements, made by striking flakes off a stone core to create a sharp edge. They predate the appearance of the genus Homo, suggesting even earlier hominins were capable toolmakers.

components.note: 夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

用's oldest forms resemble a wooden bucket or a divination tool such as a tortoise-shell frame; scholars disagree on which object it originally pictured. Either way, the character has long since become a fixed, indivisible symbol simply meaning 'to use.'

example.hanzi: 车上有一个备用轮胎。
example.pinyin: Chē shàng yǒu yí gè bèiyòng lúntāi.
example.english: There's a spare tire in the car.
example.fact: When an oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13 in 1970, the crew survived partly because NASA had built backup systems into the spacecraft and mission control engineers improvised a fix, using materials on board, to adapt a square carbon dioxide scrubber to fit a round filter socket. The mission became a textbook case for designing redundancy into critical systems.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
讠 (speech) — relates to 该's meaning 'ought to, should,' as if reached through spoken agreement.
亥 (hài) gives a sound hint — 该 is pronounced gāi, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 这本该是一个简单的任务。
example.pinyin: Zhè běngāi shì yí gè jiǎndān de rènwù.
example.english: This was supposed to be a simple task.
example.fact: In 1847, physician Ignaz Semmelweis found that maternal deaths from childbed fever in his Vienna hospital ward dropped sharply once doctors washed their hands with a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients. His colleagues largely dismissed the idea, and it was only decades after his death that handwashing became standard medical practice — a delay so infamous that resistance to obvious, well-supported findings is sometimes called the Semmelweis reflex.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 扳 (to pull, to lever) is an act done with the hand.
反 (fǎn) gives a sound distantly related to bān, sharing the same final but having drifted apart in initial consonant over time.
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 他的手指放在扳机上。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ fàng zài bānjī shàng.
example.english: His finger rested on the trigger.
example.fact: Matchlock firearms, developed in 15th-century Europe, were among the first guns to use a lever mechanism to lower a lit slow-burning cord into the flash pan, automating a job that previously required the shooter to apply fire by hand at the exact moment of firing. That lever is considered an early ancestor of the modern trigger.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
又 (a hand) — reaching out for support.
十 (a branch) — held in the hand, the image of support giving 支 its meaning 'to support, prop up; branch.'

example.hanzi: 该国严格管控枪支。
example.pinyin: Gāi guó yángé guǎnkòng qiāngzhī.
example.english: That country strictly controls guns.
example.fact: Starting in 1607, Japan's Tokugawa shogunate carried out sword and firearm confiscation edicts, known as katanagari, that sharply restricted private ownership of blades and guns for over 250 years. Historians point to that long policy as one factor behind Japan's comparatively low rates of gun ownership today.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 我们在车站分别了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài chēzhàn fēnbié le.
example.english: We parted ways at the station.
example.fact: Mantis shrimp have 12 to 16 types of photoreceptors in their eyes, compared to just three in humans, which in theory should let them distinguish far more categories of color. Oddly, behavioral tests suggest their brains process color more coarsely than the receptor count implies, and scientists are still debating exactly how they actually use this unusual visual system.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

无 is the simplified form of 無, whose oldest versions pictured a person dancing while holding decorated sleeves or tassels. That dance image was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated word 'not have, without,' and the original dancing figure is no longer recognizable in the modern simplified character.
二 is simply two horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number two, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 三 (three).

example.hanzi: 每个人的指纹都是独一无二的。
example.pinyin: Měi gèrén de zhǐwén dōu shì dúyīwú'èr de.
example.english: Everyone's fingerprints are unique.
example.fact: Physicist Kenneth Libbrecht's research on snow crystals supports the popular claim that no two snowflakes are exactly alike: each crystal falls through slightly different, constantly shifting conditions of temperature and humidity, so the branching pattern that forms is shaped by an essentially unrepeatable sequence of microscopic events.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 梅 names the plum tree.
每 (měi) gives a sound close to méi, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.
木 (tree), doubled — two trees side by side depict a cluster of trees, the source of 林's meaning 'forest, grove.'

example.hanzi: 梅林是亚瑟王传说中的魔法师。
example.pinyin: Méilín shì Yàsèwáng chuánshuō zhōng de mófǎshī.
example.english: Merlin is the wizard in the legend of King Arthur.
example.fact: The wizard Merlin was largely popularized by the 12th-century Welsh cleric Geoffrey of Monmouth in his Historia Regum Britanniae, written around 1136, which fused older Welsh folklore figures such as Myrddin Wyllt into the character familiar today. Later medieval writers, including Robert de Boron, expanded Merlin's role and tied him more closely to Arthur's story.

components.note: 辶 (a road, movement) signals that 这 is a pointing or motion-related word, used to indicate something close at hand — 'this.'
文 (wén) sits inside the simplified character as a leftover phonetic marker from an earlier form, though its sound has drifted far from zhè over the centuries.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 这时,门突然打开了。
example.pinyin: Zhè shí, mén tūrán dǎkāi le.
example.english: At that moment, the door suddenly opened.
example.fact: Einstein's 1905 theory of special relativity showed that simultaneity is not absolute: two events that appear to happen at exactly 'this moment' for one observer can appear to happen at different times for another observer moving at a different speed. The effect is imperceptible at everyday speeds but has been confirmed repeatedly using atomic clocks on fast-moving aircraft and satellites.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
门 (door/gate) — 间 pictures light passing through an entryway.
日 (sun) — sunlight shining through a gap in a doorway gave 间 its meaning of a space 'in between,' as in 中间 (in the middle) or 时间 (time, the space between moments).

example.hanzi: 传说仙女下凡来到人间。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō xiānnǚ xiàfán láidào rénjiān.
example.english: Legend says the fairy descended to the human world.
example.fact: The world's human population passed 1 billion around 1804 and has since grown to over 8 billion, with most of that increase concentrated in just the last hundred years. That surge represents one of the fastest population expansions in the roughly 300,000-year history of our species.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 娘 names a female relative, mother or young woman.
良 (liáng) gives a sound close to niáng, sharing the same rhyme.
女 (woman) — 娘 names a female relative, mother or young woman.
良 (liáng) gives a sound close to niáng, sharing the same rhyme.
⺼ (flesh) — 腔 names a hollow space inside the body.
空 (kōng) gives a sound distantly related to qiāng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 有人说他说话有点娘娘腔。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén shuō tā shuōhuà yǒudiǎn niángniangqiāng.
example.english: Some people say he talks a bit effeminately.
example.fact: Voice pitch is set largely by the length and thickness of the vocal folds: during puberty, rising testosterone thickens the folds in most male voices, dropping pitch by roughly an octave, while the resonating spaces of the throat, mouth, and nasal cavity continue to shape each person's distinct tone. Some songbird species show the reverse pattern, developing more elaborate, higher-pitched calls as they mature in order to attract mates.

components.note: 折 (to break) here suggests something that must never be broken.
言 (speech) sits below — words that must not be broken, giving 誓 its meaning 'oath, vow.'
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 他在婚礼上说出了誓言。
example.pinyin: Tā zài hūnlǐ shàng shuōchū le shìyán.
example.english: He recited his vows at the wedding.
example.fact: The Hippocratic Oath is traditionally attributed to the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates around the 5th century BC, but most medical schools today swear a heavily revised modern version rather than the original text. The phrase most people associate with it, 'first, do no harm,' does not actually appear anywhere in the ancient document.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 教练用秒表给他计时。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn yòng miǎobiǎo gěi tā jìshí.
example.english: The coach timed him with a stopwatch.
example.fact: The cesium atomic clock, built in 1955 at Britain's National Physical Laboratory, defines the second by counting oscillations of a cesium-133 atom, about 9,192,631,770 of them per second. That same precision timing underlies the GPS satellite network, which depends on atomic clocks accurate enough that even tiny errors would translate into positioning mistakes of kilometers.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嗓 names a part of the mouth/throat used for speaking.
桑 (sāng) gives a sound close to sǎng, differing only in tone.
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'

example.hanzi: 她的嗓音很好听。
example.pinyin: Tā de sǎngyīn hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: Her voice sounds very pleasant.
example.fact: Elephants communicate using extremely low-frequency rumbles, some below 20 Hz and inaudible to the human ear, that can travel several kilometers through the air and ground. Researchers have recorded elephants responding to these infrasound calls from herds that were far out of sight, suggesting the sounds help coordinate movement across long distances.

meanings: (lit.) by the thousands and tens of thousands (idiom)

components.note: 成's oldest oracle-bone form pictured a halberd, a bladed weapon on a long pole, its shaft marked with an extra stroke. The weapon image was borrowed mainly for its sound to write the unrelated word 'to become, to complete,' and the character today functions as an essentially indivisible symbol for that meaning.

千's oldest form drew a person (人) with an extra horizontal stroke through the leg, a simple mark used to distinguish the numeral 'thousand' from the plain word for 'person.' The character has stayed close to that minimal design ever since.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

万 is the simplified form of 萬, whose oldest versions are widely believed to picture a scorpion, with a rounded body and raised pincers or tail. The image was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number 'ten thousand,' and the scorpion shape is no longer visible in the modern simplified character.

example.hanzi: 成千上万的人参加了这次游行。
example.pinyin: Chéngqiānshàngwàn de rén cānjiā le zhè cì yóuxíng.
example.english: Thousands upon thousands of people took part in the march.
example.fact: Desert locust swarms can contain tens of billions of insects spread across hundreds of square kilometers, and a single large swarm can eat as much vegetation in a day as tens of thousands of people. Historically, such swarms have triggered famines across parts of Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia, and outbreaks are still tracked and forecast today by international monitoring agencies.
